LORT is just OK, to be honest. It could be some fun with friends, but to me it doesn't scratch the itch that Risk of Rain or Megabonk does. I don't feel the urge to replay this game like I do with the others.

It's not a wave by wave fight; you explore the map looking for camps of enemies. Open chests get items or gold, repeat as needed. You have 3 in-game days, which is like 20 mins, to gear up and finish the quest that then reveals the boss, defeat them or die and repeat. Movement feels slow/sluggish, even with movement items. 

I understand this is still in early development and maybe down the road it'll be better, but for right now, I'd pass on it.

Of course, this is a review and my own, and solely my own, opinion. I would recommend LORT. A lot of the negative reviews are geared towards the game either being basic or repetitive. It is an Early Access roguelite. The roguelite genre is repetitive in nature. I do agree that some other roguelites have more in depth abilities that are character specific and encourage more sets or combinations which gives them a less repetitive feel. This is still in the scope for LORT (I would assume) since the game is still in Early Access. I would also like to think that if there were more combinations or "things to chase" round to round (other than shops and the next rarity of weapon) that it would make the game feel less "basic" or "repetitive".

Some other negative reviews seemingly have less game time. Which is 100% understandable if you plan on, or may want to, get your money back. There is nothing wrong with this. With that being said. This game has an upgrade menu that gives you permanent stats that you carry with you from game to game (as long as you're on the same profile each time). So if you don't have the game time to get the materials required for upgrades... it does make things more difficult. Which, in a world of instant gratification, does come across as impossible for some. 

All in all. Personally, I think that if you have the time and happen to catch the game on sale (in the condition it is currently in) then I would give it a shot if you're a roguelite fan or just looking for a good time-killer. Also, playing with friends could be more fun (I mostly play solo or help people), especially once you get the movement and gameplay down. Keep in mind you're buying an Early Access game and have the mindset of improvement rather than what it is now and you'll enjoy yourselves.

A little opinionated side note is that most of the negative reviews seemingly sound like they just need to "get gud". Video games have basic mechanics and algorithms. Learn them and you can tilt the odds in your favor most times. The movement in this game is key and understanding how the enemies aggro and how you can move around to hit more enemies while never being hit yourself. Best of luck gamers.

Overall I would highly rate this game. I've been unable to really put it down since I bought it. With it being in development there are obvious a few cons currently, but I would honestly say it is overwhelmingly pros. The game play loop is varied enough to keep the sense of fun and achievement alive 50 hours in. 

There are also man balancing issue that need to be addressed, with certain mobs and bosses being very over-tuned when compared to the others mobs and bosses, primarily in the second and fourth zones. It's nothing that makes the game unplayable, but they can easily ruin what was otherwise a great run, more than simple "getting good".

I'm definitely excited to see where the development goes, new mobs being introduced, playable characters, bosses, narrative etc, but I'm also more than happy to plow many, many more hours into the game in it's current state.

Whenever loading the next map, the host has about a 50% chance of crashing. The game doesn't allow reconnections, making it very rare to actually complete a full playthrough. Don't bother with this game unless you have very patience friends who are willing to constantly re-join you, or the devs fix the issues.

Very fun game BUT frequently crashes when loading into the 2nd and 3rd zones. This makes playing extremely frustrating as you spend 20 minutes getting your character levelled up just to crash and starting from scratch.

The game has a lot of potential, but as is, I'd recommend purchasing and coming back in a years time. In all fairness, it's still a pretty new release however it has no fully recognized themes and after a full run or two just becomes boring. 

Difficulty scaling is absurd, bosses are unpredictable aside from vocal cues which give you close to 0 preparation for devastating attacks. It feels like you need to grind easy forever to progress in the skill tree but there is no enjoyment or satisfaction that comes from completing consecutive runs. The humor is also painfully cheap... if you're going to lean on cringe humor, truly commit to it, otherwise it becomes weird and out of place. If the bosses are clear stereotypes, why don't the levels match the tone?

I think the concept of different recipes for different final boss outcomes etc, hamming up the humor, creating more levels & also randomizing the sequence of the adventure and so on could make the game replayable, but as is, I'll tune back in once a half dozen updates roll out. Right now, it's the bones to a game that deserves more flesh.
